title: v-model: A Deeper Look
description: Explore v-model modifiers and how it works with different input types.

slides.title: v-model Recap
slides.content:
# Two‑Way Binding Made Easy

`v-model` creates a two‑way binding between a form input and a data property. It works with:
- `<input>` (text, checkbox, radio)
- `<textarea>`
- `<select>`

For text inputs, it's syntactic sugar for `:value` + `@input`:
```html
<input :value="text" @input="text = $event.target.value">
```

But `v-model` also works with other input types, each with its own handling.

slides.title: v-model Modifiers
slides.content:
# Modifiers: .lazy, .number, .trim

- **`.lazy`** – sync after `change` event instead of `input` (useful for performance).
- **`.number`** – automatically cast input to a number.
- **`.trim`** – strip leading/trailing whitespace.

```html
<input v-model.lazy="msg">
<input v-model.number="age">
<input v-model.trim="name">
```

Modifiers can be chained: `v-model.lazy.trim="text"`.

quizData.question: Which modifier would you use to update the bound property only after the input loses focus?
quizData.explanation: `.lazy` makes `v-model` sync on `change` events instead of `input`, which occurs when the input loses focus.
